issues.failure_explanation: The introduction says a family of hard instances has been constructed on which MINBERR-NE has backward error at least log(kappa)/k, and extends this to all deterministic Krylov methods. The paper contains no construction and no proof. The only support is numerical observation on one synthetic family (Small-Outlier, n=2000, limited by numerical conditioning), and Section 5 itself says only that experiments 'suggest' it. No argument covers other Krylov subspaces or methods. The GMRES-style counterexample concerns a different subspace.

failure_location.quote: we are able to construct a family of hard problem instances for which the \algne\ backward error is at least $\log(\kappa(\A))/k$ after $k$ iterations

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the introduction to say the lower bound is an empirical observation for MINBERR-NE (and normal-equations Krylov subspaces) on a synthetic family. Drop the generalization to all deterministic Krylov methods, or prove the lower bound.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised negative result (impossibility of universal rates for deterministic Krylov methods on general systems, and the log(kappa)/k lower bound) is an empirical conjecture, not an established result. The motivation for the random-perturbation variant rests on it.
issues.title: Lower bound on MINBERR-NE / any deterministic Krylov method stated as constructed fact but supported only by experiments
issues.why_classification: Rewording to an empirical, scope-limited statement fixes it without new proofs. No proved theorem is affected, although the advertised lower-bound claim is withdrawn.

issues.failure_explanation: The generalized Rayleigh quotient (eq:GRQ) drops the factor 1/||A||_2, which is harmless for the argmin. The derivation then identifies the minimum value, and the value of ||M[-1;y]||/||y|| for any y, with the backward error. The derivation actually shows ||A||_2 * berr = sigma_min(tilde T), and likewise ||A||_2 * berr(x_hat) = ||tilde T v||/||v||. The lemma, the text 'lambda_min = berr^2', Proposition prop:minberrNE and the algorithms' tests drop ||A||_2. They are correct only when ||A||_2=1, an assumption made in the proof of Theorem t:minberr but never stated here. For ||A||_2<1 the check sigma_min<epsilon does not certify berr<epsilon.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the lemma and proposition with berr = sigma_min/||A||_2 (or assume ||A||_2=1 / rescale A and b). In the algorithms compare sigma_min with epsilon times a lower bound on ||A||_2, for example ||T_k||_2, or normalize the input.
issues.overall_effect: The stopping rule and stated backward-error values of MINBERR and MINBERR-NE are off by the factor ||A||_2 unless A is pre-normalized. The tolerance guarantee 'berr < epsilon' fails when ||A||_2<1.
issues.title: MINBERR value formula omits the 1/||A||_2 factor in the backward error
issues.why_classification: A local rescaling or normalization fixes the statements and tests. The method, rates and complexity are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The constraint is that the first entry of [-1; y] equals -1. The proof shows W[0; v] = [alpha; v] with alpha = w_1[0; v]. Rescaling to first entry -1 requires multiplying by -1/alpha, so y = -v/alpha. The lemma, the proof ('the first element of (1/alpha) W[0; v] is -1', which actually equals +1), Algorithm 1, and Proposition prop:minberrNE all use +1/alpha. Check with k=1: the true minimizer over span{b} is x = b/alpha_1, whereas the formula gives -b/alpha_1, which has larger backward error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 1/alpha by -1/alpha throughout (or define alpha without the minus sign), and fix the first-entry claim in the proof and in Appendix B.
issues.overall_effect: The stated formula x_k = (1/alpha) Q_k v_min, and the final output step of Algorithms 1 and 2, return -x_k instead of the minimizer, so the output vector is not the stated MINBERR solution. The singular-value characterization and the convergence theory are unaffected.
issues.title: Sign error in recovering y (and x_k) from the singular vector
issues.why_classification: A forced sign correction in a few formulas repairs it, with no change to method or guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: For Delta=1/2 the lemma requires ell >= (1/2)[1 + ln(64 n ln(2/delta)/(pi delta^2))/ln(1.25)]. The leading coefficient is 1/(2 ln 1.25) ≈ 2.2407, which exceeds 2.23. In addition there is a dropped additive term of roughly 2.24*ln(20 ln(2/delta)) + 1/2. So 2.23 ln(k/delta^2) iterations do not satisfy the lemma's hypothesis, and for large k/delta^2 the stated count is strictly below the required one. Algorithm 1 uses this count in its while-loop.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the loop bound by the lemma's explicit expression, for example ell >= 2.25 ln(k/delta^2) + c with suitable constants, or state it as O(log(k/delta)).
issues.overall_effect: The iteration count in Algorithm 1 and the stated constant in the probability-(1-delta) factor-1.5 guarantee are not justified. The asymptotic cost O(k(T_A+n+log(1/delta))) is unaffected.
issues.title: Claimed inverse-iteration count 2.23 ln(k/delta^2) is not implied by Lemma lemma:invit
issues.why_classification: Only a numerical constant needs adjusting, with no change to the method, the guarantee or the complexity order.
